Definition: to stun, i.e. stupefy (with sleep or death)
BiblicalUsage: Radam is to stun, to stupefy — with sleep or with death. Sisera was fast asleep and weary, and Jael smote the nail into his temples; Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship, and he lay, and was fast asleep, while the storm raged; and Daniel says, 'I was in a deep sleep on my face, and my face toward the ground,' when the vision came.
TheologicalSignificance: What this says to me is that deep sleep is the Bible's picture of helplessness: Sisera could not wake, Jonah would not wake, and Daniel fell on his face — and God did His work while men slept.
